name: Sacrificial Hymn to Confucius
about: The hymn sung at the Confucian temple, as fixed by decree in 1743 and printed by J. A. van Aalst in 1884: six stanzas of eight four-syllable lines, one note to each syllable. Each syllable is written as character, gongche pitch name, and the note on Van Aalst's staff (the gongche gives the pitch, the staff its octave).
performance: Van Aalst, p. 33: the large bell sounds the first note of each verse; the bell-chime gives one sound at each word and guides the voices; after it the zithers give their note, followed by all the other instruments, and the stone-chime is struck last 'to receive the sound and transmit it' to the next note. At the end of a verse a drum is beaten three times and answered by another drum. When the hymn is finished the tiger-box is struck once and scraped. Here a verse is taken as a stanza for the drums and as a line for the large bell.
